notes:
Summary: Verdant builds an IDE copilot (VSCode & JetBrains) focused on keystroke-level completions. They are doing an evaluation of Redwood to replace a mix of hosted OpenAI + in-house model sharding. Primary ask: streaming with predictable Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and low jitter under realistic dev workloads.

Key requirements / targets (from PO & Eng call 2026-03-01):
- TTFT target: 25-40ms median for 1-2 token first-chunk responses in the editor (hard SLO for UX).
- Jitter budget: p95 < 30ms, p99 < 80ms in dev workstation region.
- Sustained throughput: support 800 concurrent active editors across a single pool with < 100ms tail for subsequent token chunks.
- Token budget controls: per-session budget (e.g. 200 tokens completion cap) + soft backpressure for continued completion streams.
- Streaming chunk size: prefer 8-32 token deltas; want ability to tune per model.
- Model/version pinning: must be able to pin stable quantized code model per team and fallback to cheaper model when dedicated capacity constrained.
- Data controls: prefer VPC + KMS; retention controls required for telemetry and snippets.

Architecture notes / wishes from Eng (Diego/CTO call):
- Client: VSCode extension implements client-side flow-control (ack per chunk) and local debounce to avoid generating on every keystroke.
- Server: want prefix/KV cache + hot-path that serves first token from cache in < 20ms when possible.
- Backpressure model: server should signal connection-level backpressure and expose token-budget errors (HTTP 429-like event) so extension can gracefully degrade.
- Batching: dynamic batching but with latency floor; need to be able to opt-out for sessions marked low-latency.
- Cost concerns: want Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization (4-bit) and batching to hit target cost per 1M tokens.

POC plan & milestones:
- Week 0: access + credentials, legal DPIA kickoff, provide VSCode plugin sample. (Done 2026-02-18)
- Week 1: integrate Redwood streaming SDK in dev env + baseline TTFT metrics (local tests). Observed median TTFT ~ 60ms with hosted demonstration config.
- Week 2: enable dedicated pool + KV caching; target to drop median to < 40ms. Measure jitter and p95.
- Week 3: token-budget pilot (200 token soft cap per completion) + client backpressure. Validate UX fallback to local static completions if budget exhausted.
- Deliverable: POC report with traces (TTFT histogram, per-chunk latency, CPU/GPU util) and recommendation for model pinning + quantization.

Recent activities timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-02-18: Intro call + demo (Samira) — noted requirement to avoid >100ms TTFT for first token.
- 2026-02-24: Security questionnaire sent (drive:/security/verdant/security-faq.md).

Quotes & paraphrases:
- "If the first token doesn't show up before the cursor blinks twice it's a dead UX." — Lead PM
- "We can accept cost tradeoffs but latency jitters kill trust; need deterministic worst-case behaviour." — Infra lead

Technical asks to Redwood SE:
- Expose TTFT traces per-request and per-region; prefer flamegraphs for token-generation path.
- Control knobs: max_chunck_tokens, stream_chunk_interval_ms, token_budget_per_session, pin_model_version, fallback_model_policy.
- Example config request: pin to rdx-code-q4k-v2 for team A, fallback to rdx-code-q8-smaller on capacity shortage; streaming chunk size 16, token_budget 200, client_ack_required=true.

Risk and blockers (notes):
- Legal requires explicit data residency proof before Dedicated contract (slows procurement).
- Their infra wants SLA for jitter; Redwood must confirm what percentiles supported on Dedicated.
- Need clarity on licensing/costs for pinned model variants (dedicated vs hosted).

Next steps (short):

- Verdant: finish internal legal checklist and share redlines by 2026-03-12.
- Schedule: end-of-POC review meeting week of 2026-03-22.
